title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's standard practices for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers as a single reference to ensure a consistent candidate and employee experience across teams.

Principles
- Candidate experience first: timely communication, clear expectations, and respectful feedback.
- Hiring for high-leverage values and skills: role fit, learning velocity, and collaboration.
- Faster cycles with quality control: measure time-to-offer and interview quality simultaneously.
- Managers enabled: provide clear templates, checklists, and decision criteria so managers can hire and develop teams reliably.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Short intro: The hiring workflow below covers role intake through offer acceptance. The people-ops team partners with hiring managers at every step to define requirements, build job descriptions, run sourcing, and ensure consistent evaluation.

Stages (standardized):
1. Role intake & approval (Owner: Hiring manager + people-ops)
   - Complete Role Intake Form (link to form). Required fields: business rationale, salary band, IC or manager level, remote/location, required vs. nice-to-have skills.
   - People-ops validates budget and role level within 3 business days.
2. Sourcing & screening (Owner: Hiring manager + recruiter)
   - Initial recruiter screen within 5 business days of role posting. Screen focuses on role fit, eligibility, and interest.
3. Interview loop (Owner: Hiring manager)
   - Typical loop: technical/skill assessment, collaboration exercise, and manager/peer interview. Include an onboarding/culture fit conversation.
   - Interview panel should include at least one cross-functional peer.
4. Decision & calibration (Owner: Hiring manager + interviewers)
   - Submit interview feedback within 48 hours. People-ops runs calibration if multiple candidates are shortlisted or senior-level roles.
5. Offer & negotiation (Owner: Hiring manager + recruiter)
   - Offer letter issued within 48 hours of decision. Target time-to-offer: <= 30 days from role post.
6. Acceptance & onboarding kickoff (Owner: recruiter + people-ops)
   - Send Welcome Packet and schedule first day sessions within 5 business days of acceptance.

Interviewer responsibilities
- Read the candidate's resume and role brief before each interview.
- Evaluate against the scorecard and provide narrative feedback.
- Avoid biased or illegal questions; refer to the interview guide for question examples.

Interviewer scorecard (use for all regular interviews)
- Core competencies (rate: 1-5): role-relevant technical skills, problem solving, communication, collaboration, ownership.
- Hire recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / No Hire.
- Notes: concrete examples, risk areas, and follow-up questions.

Decision criteria (senior and critical roles)
- For L4+ roles or roles with >$500k TCO impact: mandatory calibration meeting with people-ops and two senior engineers from other teams.
- Clear pass/fail criteria must be documented in the feedback.

Offer & negotiation steps (numbered procedure)
1. Hiring manager approves final compensation within band.
2. Recruiter drafts offer and shares with People Ops for compliance review.
3. Send offer email with PDF letter and Welcome Packet; include benefits summary and first week schedule.
4. Candidate negotiates (if applicable). Recruiter coordinates with hiring manager and People Ops; final sign-off required from People Ops for exceptions outside band.
5. Once accepted, trigger IT, security access, and payroll flows.

Time targets & metrics
- Time-to-fill (target): 45 days from posting to acceptance.
- Time-to-offer (target): 30 days.
- Recruiter response SLA: initial outreach within 3 business days.
- Interview feedback SLA: 48 hours post-interview.

2) Onboarding: First 90 days (structured plan)

Objective: Accelerate new hire productivity, build social connections, and reduce first-90-day churn. People-ops provides templates, but managers own execution.

Pre-boarding (before Day 1)
- Welcome email with first day agenda, Slack intro, and onboarding docs.
- IT account creation and provisioning checklist completed 3 business days before start.
- Assign a peer buddy and schedule 1:1s for the first two weeks.

Day 1-7 (orientation)
- Day 1: company orientation (People Ops), security and compliance briefing, benefits enrollment walkthrough.
- Team orientation: manager-led role overview, short-term expectations, and team norms.
- Setup tasks: dev environment, accounts, access to main repos and dashboards.

Weeks 2-4 (ramp)
- Clear onboarding goals (examples): complete internal / dev environment, ship first small PR, complete product and architecture readouts.
- Weekly 1:1s with manager; buddy check-ins.
- Schedule role-specific training and first project kickoff.

Months 2-3 (impact)
- Define a measurable 90-day deliverable with acceptance criteria.
- Mid-90 day check: manager does a structured progress conversation using the 90-day rubric.
- End of 90 days: written feedback from manager and buddy; update career plan.

Onboarding checklist (manager template)
- Hire packet sent: yes / no.
- Accounts provisioned: laptop, admin, Slack, SSO, CI access.
- Required training completed: security, data handling, codebase walkthrough.
- Buddy assigned and first shadow sessions scheduled.
- 90-day goals documented in performance system.

3) Performance and feedback cycles

Cycle overview
- Redwood uses a continuous feedback model with quarterly formal reviews. Managers provide ongoing feedback through 1:1s, ad-hoc notes, and structured mid-cycle check-ins. Formal reviews follow a twice-yearly calibration for salary and promotion decisions.

Cadence
- Ongoing: weekly 1:1s, monthly team syncs, quarterly manager/peer feedback collection.
- Formal reviews: mid-year and year-end (calendar-based). Calibration meetings follow each formal review cycle.

Review components
- Self-assessment: due 2 weeks prior to review.
- Manager assessment: narrative evaluation and competency ratings.
- Peer inputs: collected anonymously; focus on collaboration and impact.
- Goal progression: documented in performance system and linked to project outcomes.

Promotion & compensation decisions
- Promotion criteria: demonstrated scope increase, consistent impact, peer & manager endorsement, and readiness for the next level's responsibilities.
- Compensation adjustments are decided during calibration; People Ops provides market data and comp bands.
- Exceptional performance: managers may propose spot bonuses or ad-hoc recognition. People Ops approval required for monetary awards.

Feedback best practices for managers
- Use specific examples and impact statements.
- Balance strengths with at least one development area.
- Set clear, time-bound actions and follow-ups.
- Document feedback in the performance system within 5 business days of a formal conversation.

4) Manager playbook: hiring, onboarding, and people development

Manager responsibilities (summary)
- Own hiring decisions and provide timely feedback.
- Run effective onboarding: set expectations, goals, and check progress.
- Provide continuous coaching and career growth support.
- Escalate blockers to People Ops early (budget, role scope, or behavioral concerns).

One-on-one (1:1) cadence and agenda
- Weekly 30-60 minute 1:1 recommended for ICs; weekly for new hires during first 90 days.
- Suggested agenda: wins since last meeting, blockers, development discussion, and actionable next steps.
- Keep notes and agreed actions in the performance system or shared doc.

Career conversations and promotion readiness
- Annual career conversation separate from the formal review cycle. Reviewers should capture examples of impact, leadership, and growth.
- Promotion packet contents: promotion narrative, manager recommendation, peer feedback, and sample work. People Ops runs the promotion calibration panel.

Handling performance concerns (informal to formal)
1. Informal coaching: document conversations, set clear expectations and timeline (30-60 days).
2. Formal PIP (Performance Improvement Plan): People Ops partner required. Document goals, success criteria, and review cadence.
3. Offboarding: if outcomes are not met, follow People Ops and Legal for compliant separation steps.

5) People policies and practical guidance

Time off and leaves
- PTO accrual follows policy outlined in Benefits Summary. Managers approve discretionary PTO and escalate exceptions to People Ops.
- Parental leave, medical leave, and other protected leaves follow local law and People Ops administration.

Hybrid & remote working norms
- Teams set norms in their Team Playbook (e.g., core hours, meeting expectations). Manager documents team-specific rules at hire.

Security & data access
- Employees must complete security training during onboarding.
- Access to sensitive systems requires manager approval and an audit record in the access control system.

6) Templates, forms, and links (location references)
- Role Intake Form: /tools/role-intake (use this to start any hiring request).
- Interview Guide & Scorecard: /templates/interview-scorecard.
- Offer Letter Template: /templates/offer-letter.
- New Hire Welcome Packet: /onboarding/welcome-packet.
- 90-day Rubric & Manager Checklist: /onboarding/90-day-rubric.

Appendix: example 90-day goal template (text)
- Objective: Ship alpha of feature X to internal users.
- Success criteria: PR merged, end-to-end test coverage >= 80%, and first internal demo scheduled.
- Milestones: Week 2: environment ready, Week 4: design review complete, Week 8: integration tests passing, Week 12: demo and retrospective.

Owner & escalation
- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- For urgent hiring or performance escalations: escalate to People Ops lead and the appropriate department head.

Revision history
- 2025-06-15: created by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-10: updated to refine interview loop cadence (reviewers: Dylan Kim, Priya Reddy).
- 2026-02-10: published with updated onboarding SLA and 90-day rubric.

End of playbook. For questions or suggested updates, open a PR in the People Ops docs repo or contact People Ops via #people-ops on Slack.
